notes: Provenance: ported (issue #8) from 2AMLogic/sky130-sar-adc's
sim/pdk.json (commit b80c144efbf467a586f728726cabb25c1eb5a1f2), per
spec/porting-plan.md's 'Next steps' item 2. That file's own schema is
ported from 2AMLogic/sky130-bandgap's sim/pdk.json (commit
1f04e8524cc2d8c2c7154773749b1b2d3be2ce64), per that repo's own
'Harness bootstrap' instruction, and adapted for a sim/harness/*.py
package instead of a single sim/bin/corner-run.py script.
open_pdks_commit is the volare version hash for the sky130 PDK
family -- the SAME commit sky130-bandgap and sky130-sar-adc both
pin, kept identical across this workspace's sky130 canaries for
PVT/model provenance consistency (confirmed installed and resolvable
in this repo's own bootstrap environment via 'volare enable --pdk
sky130 c6d73a35f524070e85faff4a6a9eef49553ebc2b' -> ~/.volare/sky130A).
The harness reads $PDK_ROOT/$PDK back through its symlink and refuses
to run against a different version unless --allow-toolchain-drift is
passed (in which case the record carries the mismatch).
This file is the reproducibility pin for every record under sim/.
process_corners are the basic N/P device sections that actually exist
in the PDK ngspice library (verified against the '.lib' sections of
libs.tech/combined/sky130.lib.spice: tt, sf, ff, ss, fs, ll, hh, hl,
lh, then every one of those again with a _mm suffix). tt/ss/ff/sf/fs
are the standard MOS corners this repo's PVT runner uses by default.
ll/hh/hl/lh (resistor/capacitor-only skew corners) exist and remain
available to experiment manifests that need them but are not added to
process_corners until a manifest actually uses one.
mismatch_corners are the '_mm' local-mismatch switch: they differ
from the plain corners only in setting MC_MM_SWITCH=1, which enables
the per-instance AGAUSS() terms inside the device subcircuits (the
plain 'mc' sections instead set MC_PR_SWITCH=1, for global process
Monte Carlo -- not used by this harness). sim/monte_carlo.py drives
ngspice at a mismatch corner directly (varying only rndseed across
draws), rather than going through the PVT corner-matrix runner --
Monte Carlo sampling is not a corner axis, so sim/harness/corners.py
deliberately keeps it out of the plain process_corners list. This is
the mechanism this repo's own offset-sigma target-spec row (top-level
README, DRAFT) will eventually be measured against, per
spec/porting-plan.md.
